Question:
Show the names of the buildings that have more than one company offices.
answer: SELECT T2.name FROM Office_locations AS T1 JOIN buildings AS T2 ON T1.building_id  =  T2.id JOIN Companies AS T3 ON T1.company_id  =  T3.id GROUP BY T1.building_id HAVING COUNT(*)  >  1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from the office-location records, since each row associates a company with a building: `FROM Office_locations AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Join the building table through the building identifier so that each office record has its building name available: `JOIN buildings AS T2 ON T1.building_id = T2.id`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Join the company table through the company identifier to connect each office location to its company: `JOIN Companies AS T3 ON T1.company_id = T3.id`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Group the joined rows by building and retain only buildings associated with more than one office record: `GROUP BY T1.building_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the name of each building that satisfies the grouped count condition: `SELECT T2.name`.

what is the name and age of the youngest winning pilot?
answer: SELECT t1.name ,  t1.age FROM pilot AS t1 JOIN MATCH AS t2 ON t1.pilot_id  =  t2.winning_pilot ORDER BY t1.age LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_3: Sort the winning pilots by age from youngest to oldest; ascending order is the default: `ORDER BY t1.age`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Keep only the first row after sorting to obtain the youngest winning pilot: `LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the requested name and age columns before assembling them with the join, ordering, and limit clauses: `SELECT t1.name, t1.age`.

answer: SELECT T2.name FROM TeamsSC AS T1 INNER JOIN Teams AS T2 ON T1.tmID = T2.tmID AND T1.year = T2.year WHERE T1.year = '1917' AND T1.W > T1.L

prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the Stanley Cup statistics to the requested 1917 season: `WHERE T1.year = '1917'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Keep the team whose number of wins was greater than its number of losses: `AND T1.W > T1.L`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Return the qualifying team’s name from the joined `Teams` record using the projection: `SELECT T2.name`.

answer: SELECT COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID) FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE T1.Gender = 'M' AND T2.PersonType = 'SP'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from the employee records because `Employee` contains both the employee identifier and gender: `FROM Employee AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Join each employee to the corresponding person record so the `PersonType` classification is available: `INNER JOIN Person AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the employee records to males using the evidence-provided gender code: `WHERE T1.Gender = 'M'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Add the sales-person classification condition from the `Person` table: `AND T2.PersonType = 'SP'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Count the identifiers of employees that satisfy both conditions in the projection: `SELECT COUNT(T1.BusinessEntityID)`.

Question:
How many matches were held in the league Germany 1. Bundesliga
from August to October 2008?

Evidence:
Germany 1. Bundesliga refers to League.name = 'Germany 1. Bundesliga'; from August to October 2008 refers to strftime('%Y-%m', date) BETWEEN '2008-08' AND '2008-10';
answer: SELECT COUNT(t2.id) FROM League AS t1 INNER JOIN Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id WHERE t1.name = 'Germany 1. Bundesliga' AND SUBSTR(t2.`date`, 1, 7) BETWEEN '2008-08' AND '2008-10'

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from the league records and connect each league to its matches through the shared league identifier: `FROM League AS t1 INNER JOIN Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the joined records to the requested league using its exact name: `WHERE t1.name = 'Germany 1. Bundesliga'`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Extract the year-month portion from each match date so it can be compared with monthly boundaries: `SUBSTR(t2.`date`, 1, 7)`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Keep matches whose extracted year-month falls inclusively between August and October 2008: `AND SUBSTR(t2.`date`, 1, 7) BETWEEN '2008-08' AND '2008-10'`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Return the number of qualifying match records by counting their IDs in the projection: `SELECT COUNT(t2.id)`.

Question:

active business ID refers to active = 'true'; Goodyear is a city; Calculation = AVG(stars) * 0.8; businesses with stars greater than 80% of average star rating refers to stars > AVG(stars) * 0.8
answer: SELECT DISTINCT T2.closing_time, T3.day_of_week FROM Business AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Hours AS T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id INNER JOIN Days AS T3 ON T2.day_id = T3.day_id WHERE T1.active = 'true' AND T1.city = 'Goodyear' AND T1.stars > ( SELECT AVG(stars) * 0.8 FROM Business WHERE active = 'true' AND city = 'Goodyear' )

prefix_hints.hint_1: Link each business to its operating hours and then to the corresponding day name using the shared business and day identifiers: `FROM Business AS T1 INNER JOIN Business_Hours AS T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id INNER JOIN Days AS T3 ON T2.day_id = T3.day_id`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the outer business records to active businesses located in Goodyear: `WHERE T1.active = 'true' AND T1.city = 'Goodyear'`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Calculate 80% of the average star rating among the same active Goodyear businesses to establish the rating threshold: `SELECT AVG(stars) * 0.8 FROM Business WHERE active = 'true' AND city = 'Goodyear'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Add the threshold comparison so that only businesses whose stars exceed the calculated value qualify: `AND T1.stars > ( SELECT AVG(stars) * 0.8 FROM Business WHERE active = 'true' AND city = 'Goodyear' )`.

geographical location refers to group from SalesPerson; ComissionPct refers to commission percentage where ComissionPct > = 0.018;
answer: SELECT T1.BusinessEntityID, T2.'Group' FROM SalesPerson AS T1 INNER JOIN SalesTerritory AS T2 USING (territoryid) WHERE T1.CommissionPct >= 0.018

prefix_hints.hint_2: Link each sales person to the corresponding geographical territory through their shared territory identifier: `INNER JOIN SalesTerritory AS T2 USING (territoryid)`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Keep only business entities whose commission percentage is at least 0.018: `WHERE T1.CommissionPct >= 0.018`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Use the business entity identifier to list each qualifying company: `T1.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Build the projection with the qualifying company's identifier and its territory group as the geographical location: `SELECT T1.BusinessEntityID, T2.'Group'`.

answer: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T2.business_id) FROM Business_Hours AS T1 INNER JOIN Business AS T2 ON T1.business_id = T2.business_id INNER JOIN Business_Categories AS T3 ON T2.business_id = T3.business_id INNER JOIN Categories AS T4 ON T3.category_id = T4.category_id WHERE T2.active = 'true' AND T2.state = 'AZ' AND T1.opening_time > '12PM'

prefix_hints.hint_3: Link the category bridge to the category details using the matching category identifier: `INNER JOIN Categories AS T4 ON T3.category_id = T4.category_id`.

Question:
What is the average number of shipments done by the Kenworth trucks?

Evidence:
"Kenworth" is the make of truck; average = Divide (Count(ship_id where make = 'Kenworth'), Count(truck_id where make = 'Kenworth))
answer: SELECT CAST(COUNT(T2.ship_id) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.truck_id) FROM truck AS T1 INNER JOIN shipment AS T2 ON T1.truck_id = T2.truck_id WHERE T1.make = 'Kenworth'

prefix_hints.hint_3: Count all shipment records associated with the filtered Kenworth trucks to form the numerator: `COUNT(T2.ship_id)`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Count the distinct Kenworth trucks represented in those shipments to form the denominator: `COUNT(DISTINCT T1.truck_id)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Calculate the average shipments per Kenworth truck, casting the shipment count to REAL to preserve fractional results: `SELECT CAST(COUNT(T2.ship_id) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT T1.truck_id)`.

Question:
what is the most populated capital in the usa
answer: SELECT city_name FROM city WHERE population  =  ( SELECT MAX ( t1.population ) FROM state AS t2 JOIN city AS t1 ON t2.capital  =  t1.city_name );

prefix_hints.hint_1: Relate each state to its capital city by matching the state’s `capital` value with the city’s name: `FROM state AS t2 JOIN city AS t1 ON t2.capital = t1.city_name`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Find the greatest population among the capital cities produced by that join: `SELECT MAX(t1.population) FROM state AS t2 JOIN city AS t1 ON t2.capital = t1.city_name`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Use the `city` table as the outer query’s source so the result can return the matching city: `FROM city`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Restrict the outer city records to the population equal to the maximum capital-city population calculated by the subquery: `WHERE population = ( SELECT MAX ( t1.population ) FROM state AS t2 JOIN city AS t1 ON t2.capital = t1.city_name )`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the name of the city whose population satisfies the maximum-population condition: `SELECT city_name`.

Question:
Which religion is most prevalent in Asia?

Evidence:
Most prevalent religion refers to the religion with the most population percentage
answer: SELECT T4.Name FROM continent AS T1 INNER JOIN encompasses AS T2 ON T1.Name = T2.Continent INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN religion AS T4 ON T4.Country = T3.Code WHERE T1.Name = 'Asia' GROUP BY T4.Name ORDER BY SUM(T4.Percentage) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from continents and connect each continent to its associated countries through `encompasses`: `FROM continent AS T1 INNER JOIN encompasses AS T2 ON T1.Name = T2.Continent`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Link the encompassed country codes to the corresponding country records, then connect those countries to their religions: `INNER JOIN country AS T3 ON T3.Code = T2.Country INNER JOIN religion AS T4 ON T4.Country = T3.Code`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the joined records to countries associated with Asia: `WHERE T1.Name = 'Asia'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Combine records by religion name and rank religions by the descending sum of their population percentages: `GROUP BY T4.Name ORDER BY SUM(T4.Percentage) DESC`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Return the name of the highest-ranked religion by using the projection and one-row limit: `SELECT T4.Name` and `LIMIT 1`.

Question:
For the user who gave the most number of long reviews, what is his/her averge ratings of all review?

long reviews refers to review_length = 'long'; most number of long reviews refers to MAX(COUNT(review_length = 'long')); average ratings = AVG(review_stars);

Question:
List all the pay rates of all employees that were hired at 20 years of age.

Evidence:
pay rate refers to Rate; 20 years old at the time of being hired refers to SUBTRACT(year(HireDate)), (year(BirthDate))) = 20;
answer: SELECT T2.Rate FROM Employee AS T1 INNER JOIN EmployeePayHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) = 20

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start with the `Employee` table because it contains both the hire date and birth date needed to determine age at hiring: `FROM Employee AS T1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Link each employee to their pay history using the shared business entity identifier: `INNER JOIN EmployeePayHistory AS T2 ON T1.BusinessEntityID = T2.BusinessEntityID`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Extract the four-digit hire year with SQLite's `STRFTIME` function: `STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate)`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Identify employees hired at age 20 by subtracting their birth year from their hire year: `WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.HireDate) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.BirthDate) = 20`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Return the pay rate from each qualifying employee's pay-history record using the projection: `SELECT T2.Rate`.

metadata.evidence: pay rate refers to Rate; 20 years old at the time of being hired refers to SUBTRACT(year(HireDate)), (year(BirthDate))) = 20;

prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the first result set to students whose grade is 1: `WHERE T1.grade = 1`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Project each first-grade student's first and last names, using DISTINCT to remove duplicate rows: `SELECT DISTINCT T1.firstname, T1.lastname`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Build the set of students taught by OTHA MOYER by repeating the classroom join and filtering on the teacher's full name: `SELECT T1.firstname, T1.lastname FROM list AS T1 JOIN teachers AS T2 ON T1.classroom = T2.classroom WHERE T2.firstname = "OTHA" AND T2.lastname = "MOYER"`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Place the set-difference operator between the first-grade student query and the OTHA MOYER student query so those names are removed: `EXCEPT`.

answer: SELECT t1.organization_name FROM organizations AS t1 JOIN organization_contact_individuals AS t2 ON t1.organization_id  =  t2.organization_id GROUP BY t1.organization_name ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1

prefix_hints.hint_1: Start from the organizations table and assign the alias used to reference organization details: `FROM organizations AS t1`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Link each organization to its contact-individual records using the shared organization identifier: `JOIN organization_contact_individuals AS t2 ON t1.organization_id = t2.organization_id`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Group the joined records by organization name so each organization’s contact rows can be counted together: `GROUP BY t1.organization_name`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Sort organizations by their number of contact records in descending order, then retain only the highest-ranked organization: `ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Project the organization name for the top-ranked result by placing this clause before the joined and grouped data: `SELECT t1.organization_name`.

Question:
What is the percentage of carcinogenic molecules in triple type bonds?

Evidence:
label = '+' mean molecules are carcinogenic; triple bond refers to bond_type = '#'; percentage = DIVIDE(SUM(bond_type = '#') * 100, COUNT(bond_id)) as percent where label = '+'
answer: SELECT CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.label = '+' THEN T2.molecule_id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(DISTINCT T2.molecule_id) FROM atom AS T1 INNER JOIN molecule AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id INNER JOIN bond AS T3 ON T2.molecule_id = T3.molecule_id WHERE T3.bond_type = '#'

prefix_hints.hint_3: Restrict the joined records to triple bonds, represented by `#` in the bond type column: `WHERE T3.bond_type = '#'`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Count distinct carcinogenic molecules among the triple-bond records by conditionally retaining molecule IDs whose label is `+`: `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.label = '+' THEN T2.molecule_id ELSE NULL END)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Calculate the percentage by casting the carcinogenic-molecule count to REAL, multiplying by 100, and dividing by all distinct molecules with triple bonds: `SELECT CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T2.label = '+' THEN T2.molecule_id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(DISTINCT T2.molecule_id)`.

Question:
For all patients who are older than 55 years old, what is the percentage of female who has abnormal prothrombin time (PT)?

Evidence:
older than 55 years old = SUBTRACT(year(current_timestamp), year(Birthday)) > 55; abnormal prothrombin time (PT) refers to PT > = 14; percentage = DIVIDE(SUM(PT > = 14 AND SEX = 'F'), SUM(PT > = 14)) * 100; female refers to sex = 'F';
answer: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.PT >= 14 AND T1.SEX = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) > 55

prefix_hints.hint_1: Join each patient’s demographic information to their laboratory records using the shared patient ID: `FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID`.
prefix_hints.hint_2: Restrict the joined records to patients whose current year minus birth year is greater than 55: `WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - STRFTIME('%Y', T1.Birthday) > 55`.
prefix_hints.hint_3: Identify laboratory rows belonging to female patients with abnormal prothrombin time and count them conditionally: `SUM(CASE WHEN T2.PT >= 14 AND T1.SEX = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`.
prefix_hints.hint_4: Use the total number of qualifying joined rows as the denominator of the percentage calculation: `COUNT(*)`.
prefix_hints.hint_5: Calculate the percentage by casting the conditional count to REAL, multiplying by 100, and dividing by the total row count: `SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.PT >= 14 AND T1.SEX = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(*)`.
